their distinct authorization contracts.

### Inline media presentation

`ui/features/chat/MediaPreview.tsx` owns ordinary inline image/video presentation.
Static PNG/JPEG inline views request ephemeral `read_media_preview` binary bytes;
core derives a PNG within 768 pixels without upscaling and preserves orientation
and alpha. Encoded input is at most 16 MiB, static dimensions at most 16,777,216
pixels and decoder allocation at most 64 MiB; this is not a whole-process budget.
Optional outgoing still-image previews reuse the bounded raster-header reader in
`ui/lib/imageDimensions.ts` before creating any original-image URL. Only verified
PNG/JPEG dimensions within the same pixel ceiling are admitted; unknown,
uninspectable or excessive dimension headers retain the preparing surface. Header
inspection is not full image validation; decoder failures retain the existing
retry presentation. The existing pack
validator shares that reader and retains its own stricter pack limits.
APNG retains its original animation, and GIF/WebP/video keep their existing paths.
Current protection, expiry, consent and source identity are rechecked around work.
The host admits at most 64 queued requests and one decode. One five-second
observer deadline covers admission/runtime/pool waits; a detached parent retains
runtime ownership through the real child, and decode holds no global session
guard. An observer timeout never releases an actual worker's permits. Ordinary full-size bytes
are requested only when explicitly opened. Closing that view releases its active
original reference; failed previews never eagerly fall back to original reads and
can retry on readiness changes or foreground activation. Protected reveal remains
separate. Derived images are not persisted as plaintext or substituted for saved
originals.
Receiving, loading and unsupported states use a responsive provisional frame
(up to 320 pixels wide, 4:3 for images and 16:9 for video). Unknown outgoing
photo geometry uses a compact 192px-wide frame with a static glyph and accessible
preparation label. Outgoing photo and sticker transport state belongs to the
ordinary message footer, never a floating file-progress capsule over artwork.
Conversation rows own attachment sending feedback; `PendingGroupControls` hides
file, reaction and recall tickets in `ConversationView` while explicit management dialogs
retain status/cancellation controls. Pending message footers use an accessible
clock instead of visible sending prose; this does not change operation lifetime.
Resource-backed stickers retain their original stable 128px unframed artwork
stage across selected previews, version-skew fallbacks and canonical decode.
Ordinary Unicode emoji remain text; sending feedback must not resize sticker art.
This presentation choice does not change transport, consent, offer receipts,
byte completion, retry authority or read-only/protected access. On image decode,
the frame adopts the original aspect ratio within 320 by 320 pixels without
upscaling or cropping. Images have no padded text bubble; quoted thumbnails
fit their original ratio within 64 by 48 pixels. The lightbox retains full-size
access. Decoded image geometry is cached by live Blob URL (at most 64 entries)
so virtualized remounts can reserve the known size; initial decode may resize
a row, with reader anchors and live-edge intent owned by the viewport. Transfer readiness
must not swap an ordinary preview from a compact file card to an image row.

Image receipt uses an opaque theme surface and the image presentation of
`ReceiveProgress.tsx`. Waiting is static; a known zero remains accessible without
a visible percentage. Positive incomplete chunk counts drive a small radial
indicator, with phase-only live announcements. Complete chunk counts, local reads
and image loading retain a preparing state; file readiness alone does not reveal
the image. A current-source load reveals it with a brief opacity transition,
reduced with the user's motion preference. Cached geometry skips preparation on
remount. Load/error callbacks require current source and session ownership, and
preview failure belongs to its Blob URL so a replacement can recover. No receive
speed, stall cause, cancel action or thumbnail is inferred from chunk counts.
Ordinary file progress and attachment consent retain their existing presentation.

The ordinary-image lightbox owns pointer-anchored wheel zoom (1–8 times the
window-fit size), double-click zoom, bounded pointer dragging, fit reset and
keyboard zoom (+/−/0). Resize clamps the current position; reopening resets it.
Controls remain outside the clipped image stage. Escape restores trigger focus.
On macOS, unzoomed images retain native text selection; Option/Alt-drag bypasses
panning when zoomed. Actual recognition and selection require WKWebView evidence.
Ordinary-image context actions use the shared accessible menu, suppress WebKit
browser defaults and reuse the attachment save/reveal owners. `ui/lib/imageClipboard.ts`
# Mesh-Talk domain language

Mesh-Talk supports private conversations between authenticated participants across
local and existing routed networks, with optional peer-operated encrypted custody.
This is the canonical glossary; [DDD conventions](docs/domain-design.md) own its
use in code, ownership decisions and documentation.

## Identity and access

**Local user**:
A local sign-in identity and its protected application data. A local user is not
the cross-device mesh account or a network device.
_Avoid_: account ID, device ID when referring to the local login identity.

**Username / account login name**:
The name entered at sign-in. Linked desktop devices use the kept account's same
login name and password. It is distinct from the account nickname and from the
immutable local storage username retained internally for an existing local user.
_Avoid_: account ID, device ID, nickname, storage directory as interchangeable names.

**Local storage username**:
The existing per-device storage namespace for a local user. Account login
migration preserves this name and the local-user UUID; a credential envelope maps
the shared login to the retained local owner and its separate storage secrets.
_Avoid_: account login name, account ID, shared password.

**Display name**:
A human-readable label for presentation. It is neither unique identity nor
proof of authority.
_Avoid_: identifier, verified identity.

**Account**:
A cryptographic identity shared across certified devices. Account identity does
not depend on a desktop login, IP address or display name.
_Avoid_: local user, machine, device.

**Account profile**:
Account-authenticated nickname, biography and avatar, saved through ordinary
profile editing and synchronized automatically. It carries read-only creation
metadata when known; revisions order updates across devices.
_Avoid_: local login profile, device identity, proof of a person's identity.

Linked devices share account login credentials through private account access. Login names remain distinct from public nicknames; device identities and local encrypted-storage secrets remain distinct.

**Device**:
A participant identified by its persistent signing and key-agreement identity.
Restarting a process does not by itself create a new device.
_Avoid_: running instance, account, physical computer.

**Device certificate**:
An account-signed binding of a device's public identity to that account.
_Avoid_: discovery record, membership grant.

**Account group role**:
The account's accepted member or owner role in a channel. Certified devices
present the same account role. The public membership state and verified account
bindings establish that role; device reachability determines execution
availability, not a different role. Legacy public controls retain their existing
signer requirements.
_Avoid_: online status, device approval, shared group reference.

**Account group operation**:
An account-authorized intent to change channel state or send channel content.
Its pending identity is distinct from the public events that commit its effects.
Execution may use an authorized device without changing the account's role or
reattributing existing public events.
_Avoid_: committed event before acceptance, device-specific permission.

**Peer**:
Another known network device, including an infrastructure device when the role
permits it. A peer is not necessarily a person or a channel member.
_Avoid_: user, contact, member as interchangeable names.

**Contact**:
An account represented in local conversation/contact state. Contact visibility
is separate from discovery, delivery permission and channel membership.
Automatic [never-chatted contact expiry](docs/privacy-controls.md#discovered-contacts-without-chat-history)
is a local presentation policy, distinct from personal conversation removal.
_Avoid_: online peer, accepted member.

**Desktop session**:
One authenticated local user's login lifetime. A subsequent login starts a new
lifetime even when it belongs to the same local user.
_Avoid_: transport session, ratchet session, account lifetime.

**Participant runtime**:
The active network-participation lifetime of an initialized node. It is distinct
from persistent device identity and the host's login lifetime.
_Avoid_: device, desktop session.

**Integration grant**:
An authorization for a local client to perform specified integration operations
for permitted destinations within its validity period.
_Avoid_: channel membership, device certificate, session token.

## Conversations and history

**Personal conversation removal**:
An account-private decision to remove a chat, optionally erasing its history on
certified linked devices. Durable deletion floors prevent stale private replay;
each device confirms its own cleanup separately. It is distinct from leaving or
dissolving a group, recalling a message and blocking a contact.
_Avoid_: global deletion, completed cleanup based only on a committed group Leave.
See [removal semantics](docs/network-design-reference.md#personal-conversation-removal).

**Conversation**:
A direct or channel conversation whose authorized content can be retained and
synchronized. A UI conversation selection is a view of that conversation.
_Avoid_: transport connection, multicast group.

**Direct message (DM)**:
A message in a direct conversation between account or legacy device identities.
It is not necessarily transmitted over a direct network route.
_Avoid_: direct connection, LAN-only message.

**Channel**:
A conversation governed by signed membership and control state. “Group” is an
accepted user-facing label for this concept.
_Avoid_: multicast group, Noise channel when referring to conversation membership.

**Channel member**:
A signed account grant admitted by the channel's membership state. Certified
devices inherit that account's accepted membership and role without another owner
approval. Legacy channels retain device-scoped authority until a validated,
owner-signed account migration; discovery alone never creates membership.
_Avoid_: discovered peer, invitee, online person.

**Event**:
An immutable, signed, content-addressed protocol record with authenticated
ancestry. Events can represent messages, reactions, membership changes or other
protocol facts; not every event is a user-visible message.
_Avoid_: UI notification, IPC callback, message as a universal synonym.

**Message**:
Conversation content presented as one logical message. Pending UI content and
protocol records are different representations, not interchangeable identities.
_Avoid_: Event ID before acceptance, transport frame.

**Logical file message**:
One accepted file or sticker send, identified independently of its per-device
signed manifests. An authenticated sender binding can associate those exact
manifests with the same logical message. Repeated sends remain separate messages
even when they reuse the same encrypted transfer or have identical artwork.
_Avoid_: file-conversation ID, checksum, timestamp or device-manifest ID as an
interchangeable message identity.

**Device file manifest**:
A signed file offer for one destination device. Its exact event identity remains
authoritative for that device's consent and completion, even when history
projects a shared logical file message.
_Avoid_: logical file message, completed image bytes.

**Outgoing intent**:
A local attempt to send content to a conversation before or while acceptance is
resolved. Its local identity is distinct from an accepted event's identity.
_Avoid_: delivered message, accepted event before acceptance.

**Protected message**:
A text or image message carrying an authenticated requirement to conceal its content
until an explicit local reveal, optionally after the viewer authenticates with
the application's lock mechanism. Each reveal lasts at most 30 seconds on that
device. Protection is separate from retention, message expiry and read state.
_Avoid_: disappearing message, view-once message, password shared by the sender.

**History coverage**:
What this installation has observed of a conversation's retained events. It is
not proof of global history completeness or a read position.
_Avoid_: synchronization complete, all messages received.

**Message Yourself**:
The current account's personal conversation. Its existence does not require a
second device to be discoverable.
UI label: **Message Yourself** (Simplified Chinese: **给自己发消息**).
_Avoid_: second account, temporary local scratch chat.

**Forwarded message**:
A new message sent by the forwarding account using authorized retained source
content. It has its own destination identity and delivery lifecycle. A merged
chat record contains historical display snapshots attributed by the forwarder;
those labels are not new signatures by the historical authors.

# Writing Plans

## Overview

Write comprehensive implementation plans assuming the engineer has zero context for our codebase and questionable taste. Document everything they need to know: which files to touch for each task, code, testing, docs they might need to check, how to test it. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.

Assume they are a skilled developer, but know almost nothing about our toolset or problem domain. Assume they don't know good test design very well.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."

**Context:** This should be run in a dedicated worktree (created by brainstorming skill).

**Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`
- (User preferences for plan location override this default)

## Scope Check

If the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans — one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.

## File Structure

Before defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.

- Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.
- You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.
- Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.
- In existing codebases, follow established patterns. If the codebase uses large files, don't unilaterally restructure - but if a file you're modifying has grown unwieldy, including a split in the plan is reasonable.

This structure informs the task decomposition. Each task should produce self-contained changes that make sense independently.

## Bite-Sized Task Granularity

**Each step is one action (2-5 minutes):**
- "Write the failing test" - step
- "Run it to make sure it fails" - step
- "Implement the minimal code to make the test pass" - step
- "Run the tests and make sure they pass" - step
- "Commit" - step

## Plan Document Header

**Every plan MUST start with this header:**

```markdown
# [Feature Name] Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]

**Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]

**Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]

---
```

## Task Structure

````markdown
### Task N: [Component Name]

**Files:**
- Create: `exact/path/to/file.py`
- Modify: `exact/path/to/existing.py:123-145`
- Test: `tests/exact/path/to/test.py`

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

```python
def test_specific_behavior():
    result = function(input)
    assert result == expected
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Run test to verify it fails**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: FAIL with "function not defined"

- [ ] **Step 3: Write minimal implementation**

```python
def function(input):
    return expected
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Run test to verify it passes**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: PASS

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add tests/path/test.py src/path/file.py
git commit -m "feat: add specific feature"
```
````

## No Placeholders

Every step must contain the actual content an engineer needs. These are **plan failures** — never write them:
- "TBD", "TODO", "implement later", "fill in details"
- "Add appropriate error handling" / "add validation" / "handle edge cases"
- "Write tests for the above" (without actual test code)
- "Similar to Task N" (repeat the code — the engineer may be reading tasks out of order)
- Steps that describe what to do without showing how (code blocks required for code steps)
- References to types, functions, or methods not defined in any task

## Remember
- Exact file paths always
- Complete code in every step — if a step changes code, show the code
- Exact commands with expected output
- DRY, YAGNI, TDD, frequent commits

## Self-Review

After writing the complete plan, look at the spec with fresh eyes and check the plan against it. This is a checklist you run yourself — not a subagent dispatch.

**1. Spec coverage:** Skim each section/requirement in the spec. Can you point to a task that implements it? List any gaps.

**2. Placeholder scan:** Search your plan for red flags — any of the patterns from the "No Placeholders" section above. Fix them.

**3. Type consistency:** Do the types, method signatures, and property names you used in later tasks match what you defined in earlier tasks? A function called `clearLayers()` in Task 3 but `clearFullLayers()` in Task 7 is a bug.

If you find issues, fix them inline. No need to re-review — just fix and move on. If you find a spec requirement with no task, add the task.

## Execution Handoff

After saving the plan, offer execution choice:

**"Plan complete and saved to `docs/superpowers/plans/<filename>.md`. Two execution options:**

**1. Subagent-Driven (recommended)** - I dispatch a fresh subagent per task, review between tasks, fast iteration

# Verification Before Completion

## Overview

Claiming work is complete without verification is dishonesty, not efficiency.

**Core principle:** Evidence before claims, always.

**Violating the letter of this rule is violating the spirit of this rule.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO COMPLETION CLAIMS WITHOUT FRESH VERIFICATION EVIDENCE
```

If you haven't run the verification command in this message, you cannot claim it passes.

## The Gate Function

```
BEFORE claiming any status or expressing satisfaction:

1. IDENTIFY: What command proves this claim?
2. RUN: Execute the FULL command (fresh, complete)
3. READ: Full output, check exit code, count failures
4. VERIFY: Does output confirm the claim?
   - If NO: State actual status with evidence
   - If YES: State claim WITH evidence
5. ONLY THEN: Make the claim

Skip any step = lying, not verifying
```

## Common Failures

| Claim | Requires | Not Sufficient |
|-------|----------|----------------|
| Tests pass | Test command output: 0 failures | Previous run, "should pass" |
| Linter clean | Linter output: 0 errors | Partial check, extrapolation |
| Build succeeds | Build command: exit 0 | Linter passing, logs look good |
| Bug fixed | Test original symptom: passes | Code changed, assumed fixed |
| Regression test works | Red-green cycle verified | Test passes once |
| Agent completed | VCS diff shows changes | Agent reports "success" |
| Requirements met | Line-by-line checklist | Tests passing |

## Red Flags - STOP

- Using "should", "probably", "seems to"
- Expressing satisfaction before verification ("Great!", "Perfect!", "Done!", etc.)
- About to commit/push/PR without verification
- Trusting agent success reports
- Relying on partial verification
- Thinking "just this once"
- Tired and wanting work over
- **ANY wording implying success without having run verification**

## Rationalization Prevention

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Should work now" | RUN the verification |
| "I'm confident" | Confidence ≠ evidence |
| "Just this once" | No exceptions |
| "Linter passed" | Linter ≠ compiler |
| "Agent said success" | Verify independently |
| "I'm tired" | Exhaustion ≠ excuse |
| "Partial check is enough" | Partial proves nothing |
| "Different words so rule doesn't apply" | Spirit over letter |

## Key Patterns

**Tests:**
```
✅ [Run test command] [See: 34/34 pass] "All tests pass"
❌ "Should pass now" / "Looks correct"
```

**Regression tests (TDD Red-Green):**
```
✅ Write → Run (pass) → Revert fix → Run (MUST FAIL) → Restore → Run (pass)
❌ "I've written a regression test" (without red-green verification)
```

**Build:**
```
✅ [Run build] [See: exit 0] "Build passes"
❌ "Linter passed" (linter doesn't check compilation)
```

**Requirements:**
```
✅ Re-read plan → Create checklist → Verify each → Report gaps or completion
❌ "Tests pass, phase complete"
```

**Agent delegation:**
```
✅ Agent reports success → Check VCS diff → Verify changes → Report actual state
❌ Trust agent report
```

## Why This Matters

From 24 failure memories:
- your human partner said "I don't believe you" - trust broken
- Undefined functions shipped - would crash
- Missing requirements shipped - incomplete features
- Time wasted on false completion → redirect → rework
- Violates: "Honesty is a core value. If you lie, you'll be replaced."

## When To Apply

**ALWAYS before:**
- ANY variation of success/completion claims
- ANY expression of satisfaction
- ANY positive statement about work state
- Committing, PR creation, task completion
- Moving to next task
- Delegating to agents

**Rule applies to:**
- Exact phrases
- Paraphrases and synonyms
- Implications of success
- ANY communication suggesting completion/correctness

## The Bottom Line

**No shortcuts for verification.**

Run the command. Read the output. THEN claim the result.

This is non-negotiable.

# Module Ownership and Reuse

This is the implementation ownership map for maintaining Mesh Talk and assigning
parallel work. Use it to locate the owner of a decision before adding another
implementation. Network semantics and configuration belong to the
[communication architecture](network-design-reference.md); this document defines
where those decisions live in code and how to change them safely.

The [canonical glossary](../CONTEXT.md) defines domain concepts;
[DDD conventions](domain-design.md) define modeling terms and identifier mappings.
The layers and owners below are implementation responsibilities, not declarations
that every module or crate is a separate DDD bounded context.

## 1. Dependency direction

| Desktop host: `src-tauri`                   | Session/runtime installation, OS integration, settings persistence, authorized IPC adaptation | Core public exports                                     | Wire validation, cryptographic authority and delivery state machines |
| Typed IPC: `frontend/src/lib/api`           | Command names, payload shapes, typed results                                                  | Shared types, Tauri APIs and sibling adapters           | UI stores, React features and business decisions                     |
| Application stores: `frontend/src/store`    | Reactive state, owner-scoped work, optimistic intents, cache transitions                      | Typed adapters and shared projections                   | Core authority and feature rendering                                 |
| Feature modules: `frontend/src/features`    | User interaction and composition                                                              | Stores, typed adapters, shared models and UI primitives | Reimplementation of identity, policy or delivery rules               |
| UI primitives: `frontend/src/components/ui` | Accessible visual controls                                                                    | React/Radix and styling helpers                         | Session lifecycle and protocol policy                                |

The bot integration service in `crates/mesh-talk-integrations` depends on the core
and host-supplied admission ports. It owns grants, bounded metadata audit and

# Mesh-Talk domain language

Mesh-Talk supports private conversations between authenticated participants across
local and existing routed networks, with optional peer-operated encrypted custody.
This is the canonical glossary; [DDD conventions](docs/domain-design.md) own its
use in code, ownership decisions and documentation.

## Identity and access

**Local user**:
A local sign-in identity and its protected application data. A local user is not
the cross-device mesh account or a network device.
_Avoid_: account ID, device ID when referring to the local login identity.

**Username / account login name**:
The name entered at sign-in. Linked desktop devices use the kept account's same
login name and password. It is distinct from the account nickname and from the
immutable local storage username retained internally for an existing local user.
_Avoid_: account ID, device ID, nickname, storage directory as interchangeable names.

**Local storage username**:
The existing per-device storage namespace for a local user. Account login
migration preserves this name and the local-user UUID; a credential envelope maps
the shared login to the retained local owner and its separate storage secrets.
_Avoid_: account login name, account ID, shared password.

**Display name**:
A human-readable label for presentation. It is neither unique identity nor
proof of authority.
_Avoid_: identifier, verified identity.

**Account**:
A cryptographic identity shared across certified devices. Account identity does
not depend on a desktop login, IP address or display name.
_Avoid_: local user, machine, device.

**Account profile**:
Account-authenticated nickname, biography and avatar, saved through ordinary
profile editing and synchronized automatically. It carries read-only creation
metadata when known; revisions order updates across devices.
_Avoid_: local login profile, device identity, proof of a person's identity.

Linked devices share account login credentials through private account access. Login names remain distinct from public nicknames; device identities and local encrypted-storage secrets remain distinct.

**Device**:
A participant identified by its persistent signing and key-agreement identity.
Restarting a process does not by itself create a new device.
_Avoid_: running instance, account, physical computer.

**Device certificate**:
An account-signed binding of a device's public identity to that account.
_Avoid_: discovery record, membership grant.

**Account group role**:
The account's accepted member or owner role in a channel. Certified devices
present the same account role. The public membership state and verified account
bindings establish that role; device reachability determines execution
availability, not a different role. Legacy public controls retain their existing
signer requirements.
_Avoid_: online status, device approval, shared group reference.

**Account group operation**:
An account-authorized intent to change channel state or send channel content.
Its pending identity is distinct from the public events that commit its effects.
Execution may use an authorized device without changing the account's role or
reattributing existing public events.
_Avoid_: committed event before acceptance, device-specific permission.

**Peer**:
Another known network device, including an infrastructure device when the role
permits it. A peer is not necessarily a person or a channel member.
_Avoid_: user, contact, member as interchangeable names.

**Contact**:
An account represented in local conversation/contact state. Contact visibility
is separate from discovery, delivery permission and channel membership.
Automatic [never-chatted contact expiry](docs/privacy-controls.md#discovered-contacts-without-chat-history)
is a local presentation policy, distinct from personal conversation removal.
_Avoid_: online peer, accepted member.

**Desktop session**:
One authenticated local user's login lifetime. A subsequent login starts a new
lifetime even when it belongs to the same local user.
_Avoid_: transport session, ratchet session, account lifetime.

**Participant runtime**:
The active network-participation lifetime of an initialized node. It is distinct
from persistent device identity and the host's login lifetime.
_Avoid_: device, desktop session.

**Integration grant**:
An authorization for a local client to perform specified integration operations
for permitted destinations within its validity period.
_Avoid_: channel membership, device certificate, session token.

## Conversations and history

**Personal conversation removal**:
An account-private decision to remove a chat, optionally erasing its history on
certified linked devices. Durable deletion floors prevent stale private replay;
each device confirms its own cleanup separately. It is distinct from leaving or
dissolving a group, recalling a message and blocking a contact.
_Avoid_: global deletion, completed cleanup based only on a committed group Leave.
See [removal semantics](docs/network-design-reference.md#personal-conversation-removal).

**Conversation**:
A direct or channel conversation whose authorized content can be retained and
synchronized. A UI conversation selection is a view of that conversation.
_Avoid_: transport connection, multicast group.

**Direct message (DM)**:
A message in a direct conversation between account or legacy device identities.
It is not necessarily transmitted over a direct network route.
_Avoid_: direct connection, LAN-only message.

**Channel**:
A conversation governed by signed membership and control state. “Group” is an
accepted user-facing label for this concept.
_Avoid_: multicast group, Noise channel when referring to conversation membership.

**Channel member**:
A signed account grant admitted by the channel's membership state. Certified
devices inherit that account's accepted membership and role without another owner
approval. Legacy channels retain device-scoped authority until a validated,
owner-signed account migration; discovery alone never creates membership.
_Avoid_: discovered peer, invitee, online person.

**Event**:
An immutable, signed, content-addressed protocol record with authenticated
ancestry. Events can represent messages, reactions, membership changes or other
protocol facts; not every event is a user-visible message.
_Avoid_: UI notification, IPC callback, message as a universal synonym.

**Message**:
Conversation content presented as one logical message. Pending UI content and
protocol records are different representations, not interchangeable identities.
_Avoid_: Event ID before acceptance, transport frame.

**Logical file message**:
One accepted file or sticker send, identified independently of its per-device
signed manifests. An authenticated sender binding can associate those exact
manifests with the same logical message. Repeated sends remain separate messages
even when they reuse the same encrypted transfer or have identical artwork.
_Avoid_: file-conversation ID, checksum, timestamp or device-manifest ID as an
interchangeable message identity.

**Device file manifest**:
A signed file offer for one destination device. Its exact event identity remains
authoritative for that device's consent and completion, even when history
projects a shared logical file message.
_Avoid_: logical file message, completed image bytes.

**Outgoing intent**:
A local attempt to send content to a conversation before or while acceptance is
resolved. Its local identity is distinct from an accepted event's identity.
_Avoid_: delivered message, accepted event before acceptance.

**Protected message**:
A text or image message carrying an authenticated requirement to conceal its content
until an explicit local reveal, optionally after the viewer authenticates with
the application's lock mechanism. Each reveal lasts at most 30 seconds on that
device. Protection is separate from retention, message expiry and read state.
_Avoid_: disappearing message, view-once message, password shared by the sender.

**History coverage**:
What this installation has observed of a conversation's retained events. It is
not proof of global history completeness or a read position.
_Avoid_: synchronization complete, all messages received.

**Message Yourself**:
The current account's personal conversation. Its existence does not require a
second device to be discoverable.
UI label: **Message Yourself** (Simplified Chinese: **给自己发消息**).
_Avoid_: second account, temporary local scratch chat.

**Forwarded message**:
A new message sent by the forwarding account using authorized retained source
content. It has its own destination identity and delivery lifecycle. A merged
chat record contains historical display snapshots attributed by the forwarder;
those labels are not new signatures by the historical authors.

# Writing Plans

## Overview

Write comprehensive implementation plans assuming the engineer has zero context for our codebase and questionable taste. Document everything they need to know: which files to touch for each task, code, testing, docs they might need to check, how to test it. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.

Assume they are a skilled developer, but know almost nothing about our toolset or problem domain. Assume they don't know good test design very well.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."

**Context:** This should be run in a dedicated worktree (created by brainstorming skill).

**Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`
- (User preferences for plan location override this default)

## Scope Check

If the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans — one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.

## File Structure

Before defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.

- Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.
- You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.
- Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.
- In existing codebases, follow established patterns. If the codebase uses large files, don't unilaterally restructure - but if a file you're modifying has grown unwieldy, including a split in the plan is reasonable.

This structure informs the task decomposition. Each task should produce self-contained changes that make sense independently.

## Bite-Sized Task Granularity

**Each step is one action (2-5 minutes):**
- "Write the failing test" - step
- "Run it to make sure it fails" - step
- "Implement the minimal code to make the test pass" - step
- "Run the tests and make sure they pass" - step
- "Commit" - step

## Plan Document Header

**Every plan MUST start with this header:**

```markdown
# [Feature Name] Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]

**Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]

**Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]

---
```

## Task Structure

````markdown
### Task N: [Component Name]

**Files:**
- Create: `exact/path/to/file.py`
- Modify: `exact/path/to/existing.py:123-145`
- Test: `tests/exact/path/to/test.py`

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

```python
def test_specific_behavior():
    result = function(input)
    assert result == expected
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Run test to verify it fails**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: FAIL with "function not defined"

- [ ] **Step 3: Write minimal implementation**

```python
def function(input):
    return expected
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Run test to verify it passes**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: PASS

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add tests/path/test.py src/path/file.py
git commit -m "feat: add specific feature"
```
````

## No Placeholders

Every step must contain the actual content an engineer needs. These are **plan failures** — never write them:
- "TBD", "TODO", "implement later", "fill in details"
- "Add appropriate error handling" / "add validation" / "handle edge cases"
- "Write tests for the above" (without actual test code)
- "Similar to Task N" (repeat the code — the engineer may be reading tasks out of order)
- Steps that describe what to do without showing how (code blocks required for code steps)
- References to types, functions, or methods not defined in any task

## Remember
- Exact file paths always
- Complete code in every step — if a step changes code, show the code
- Exact commands with expected output
- DRY, YAGNI, TDD, frequent commits

## Self-Review

After writing the complete plan, look at the spec with fresh eyes and check the plan against it. This is a checklist you run yourself — not a subagent dispatch.

**1. Spec coverage:** Skim each section/requirement in the spec. Can you point to a task that implements it? List any gaps.

**2. Placeholder scan:** Search your plan for red flags — any of the patterns from the "No Placeholders" section above. Fix them.

**3. Type consistency:** Do the types, method signatures, and property names you used in later tasks match what you defined in earlier tasks? A function called `clearLayers()` in Task 3 but `clearFullLayers()` in Task 7 is a bug.

If you find issues, fix them inline. No need to re-review — just fix and move on. If you find a spec requirement with no task, add the task.

## Execution Handoff

After saving the plan, offer execution choice:

**"Plan complete and saved to `docs/superpowers/plans/<filename>.md`. Two execution options:**

**1. Subagent-Driven (recommended)** - I dispatch a fresh subagent per task, review between tasks, fast iteration

**2. Inline Execution** - Execute tasks in this session using executing-plans, batch execution with checkpoints

**Which approach?"**

**If Subagent-Driven chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development
- Fresh subagent per task + two-stage review

**If Inline Execution chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:executing-plans
- Batch execution with checkpoints for review

name: verification-before-completion
description: Use when about to claim work is complete, fixed, or passing, before committing or creating PRs - requires running verification commands and confirming output before making any success claims; evidence before assertions always
---

# Verification Before Completion

## Overview

Claiming work is complete without verification is dishonesty, not efficiency.

**Core principle:** Evidence before claims, always.

**Violating the letter of this rule is violating the spirit of this rule.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO COMPLETION CLAIMS WITHOUT FRESH VERIFICATION EVIDENCE
```

If you haven't run the verification command in this message, you cannot claim it passes.

## The Gate Function

```
BEFORE claiming any status or expressing satisfaction:

1. IDENTIFY: What command proves this claim?
2. RUN: Execute the FULL command (fresh, complete)
3. READ: Full output, check exit code, count failures
4. VERIFY: Does output confirm the claim?
   - If NO: State actual status with evidence
   - If YES: State claim WITH evidence
5. ONLY THEN: Make the claim

Skip any step = lying, not verifying
```

## Common Failures

| Claim | Requires | Not Sufficient |
|-------|----------|----------------|
| Tests pass | Test command output: 0 failures | Previous run, "should pass" |
| Linter clean | Linter output: 0 errors | Partial check, extrapolation |
| Build succeeds | Build command: exit 0 | Linter passing, logs look good |
| Bug fixed | Test original symptom: passes | Code changed, assumed fixed |
| Regression test works | Red-green cycle verified | Test passes once |
| Agent completed | VCS diff shows changes | Agent reports "success" |
| Requirements met | Line-by-line checklist | Tests passing |

## Red Flags - STOP

- Using "should", "probably", "seems to"
- Expressing satisfaction before verification ("Great!", "Perfect!", "Done!", etc.)
- About to commit/push/PR without verification
- Trusting agent success reports
- Relying on partial verification
- Thinking "just this once"
- Tired and wanting work over
- **ANY wording implying success without having run verification**

## Rationalization Prevention

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Should work now" | RUN the verification |
| "I'm confident" | Confidence ≠ evidence |
| "Just this once" | No exceptions |
| "Linter passed" | Linter ≠ compiler |
| "Agent said success" | Verify independently |
| "I'm tired" | Exhaustion ≠ excuse |
| "Partial check is enough" | Partial proves nothing |
| "Different words so rule doesn't apply" | Spirit over letter |

## Key Patterns

**Tests:**
```
✅ [Run test command] [See: 34/34 pass] "All tests pass"
❌ "Should pass now" / "Looks correct"
```

**Regression tests (TDD Red-Green):**
```
✅ Write → Run (pass) → Revert fix → Run (MUST FAIL) → Restore → Run (pass)
❌ "I've written a regression test" (without red-green verification)
```

**Build:**
```
✅ [Run build] [See: exit 0] "Build passes"
❌ "Linter passed" (linter doesn't check compilation)
```

**Requirements:**
```
✅ Re-read plan → Create checklist → Verify each → Report gaps or completion
❌ "Tests pass, phase complete"
```

**Agent delegation:**
```
✅ Agent reports success → Check VCS diff → Verify changes → Report actual state
❌ Trust agent report
```

## Why This Matters

From 24 failure memories:
- your human partner said "I don't believe you" - trust broken
- Undefined functions shipped - would crash
- Missing requirements shipped - incomplete features
- Time wasted on false completion → redirect → rework
- Violates: "Honesty is a core value. If you lie, you'll be replaced."

## When To Apply

**ALWAYS before:**
- ANY variation of success/completion claims
- ANY expression of satisfaction
- ANY positive statement about work state
- Committing, PR creation, task completion
- Moving to next task
- Delegating to agents

**Rule applies to:**
- Exact phrases
- Paraphrases and synonyms
- Implications of success
- ANY communication suggesting completion/correctness

## The Bottom Line

**No shortcuts for verification.**

Run the command. Read the output. THEN claim the result.

This is non-negotiable.
"}

# Implementation status and acceptance boundaries

This stable path is the current status index, not a chronological TODO list or a
claim that every topology/platform combination has been verified. Feature and
protocol details belong to the linked owning guides; Git history records completed
work.

## Current capability areas

| Area                       | Implemented behavior                                                                                                                             | Reference / boundary                                                                                                                                                                    |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Direct conversations       | Signed discovery, identity-pinned Noise/TCP, encrypted account-addressed DMs, replies, reactions, mentions, search and retained history.         | [Architecture](../docs/ARCHITECTURE.md); discovery and TCP reachability remain separate.                                                                                                |
| Groups                     | Signed membership controls, sender-key encryption, bounded fanout and authorized member recovery with per-member sharing.                        | [Group flows and scenarios](../docs/network-design-reference.md#d-group-creation-distribution-and-member-recovery); a removed/nonmember device cannot acquire authority from discovery. |
| Relay networking           | Equal trusted post offices, shared public enrollment, opaque custody/federation, direct-first attempts, soft preference and alternatives.        | [Network baseline](../docs/network-design-reference.md); an alternate needs a surviving onward route.                                                                                   |
| Network controls           | Per-device master/send/receive/directory preferences, physical-LAN-only discovery and direct LAN/Tailscale relay selection.                      | [Privacy controls](../docs/privacy-controls.md); visibility does not grant conversation authority or create a firewall.                                                                 |
| Files and folders          | Encrypted chunks, exact-offer consent, durable decisions, restart recovery, integrity checks and recipient completion.                           | [File flow](../docs/network-design-reference.md#e-files-folders-consent-and-completion); card arrival is not byte completion.                                                           |
| Linked devices             | Code-authorized enrollment, certified sibling synchronization and device-local category preferences.                                             | [Pairing and replay](../docs/network-design-reference.md#g-linking-and-ongoing-account-synchronization); full replay needs its own live authenticated route.                            |
| Calls                      | Optional device-addressed live Noise signaling and separate WebRTC media.                                                                        | No post-office signaling fallback or TURN service; native WebView and physical capture acceptance remain separate.                                                                      |
| Desktop presentation       | Shared person/relay classification, account/device profile details, themes, avatars, stickers, virtualized navigation and optional pack installation. | [Visual system](../frontend/DESIGN.md) · [Customization packs](../docs/CUSTOMIZATION_PACKS.md).                                                                                         |
| Local privacy and recovery | Privacy presets, lock controls, hidden contacts, local retention, recall and encrypted manual backup/restore.                                    | [Privacy](../docs/privacy-controls.md) · [Backup/recovery](../docs/backup-recovery.md); restore creates a new device and cannot revoke an old one.                                      |

## Deliberate design boundaries

- **Pairing authorization:** a one-time 128-bit code binds the linker and joiner
  device keys. Durable enrollment invalidates old sessions; interrupted adoption
  has a restricted code-authenticated retry. There is no separate SAS ceremony.
- **Relay metadata:** production relays store opaque outer events, not readable
  original authors, conversation IDs or channel controls. Connection identities,
  pseudonymous mailboxes, size buckets and timing remain observable. See
  [the exact privacy boundary](../docs/post-office-metadata-privacy.md).
- **Bounded custody:** relay copies have capacity limits and a 30-day maximum age;
  this is not guaranteed minimum retention or permanent storage.
- **Connections:** the client Node has bounded sequential session reuse, not one
  multiplexed socket per relay or an eight-socket ceiling for the whole machine.
- **Reachability and trust:** Tailscale does not merge LANs; explicit relay trust
  and client directory consent are independent of routing.
- **Membership presentation:** removed group members' past reactions no longer
  render under the current-membership visibility rule.
- **Linux dependency constraint:** the maintained
  [GLib compatibility workflow](../.github/workflows/glib-0.20-watch.yml) tracks the
  GTK/Tauri dependency gate. Consult the lockfile and security configuration before
  changing versions; do not treat this note as a vulnerability waiver.

## Evidence and future decisions

The [implementation/evidence tracker](../docs/network-design-reference.md#implementation-and-evidence-tracker)
records named logical and physical checks. Three independent physical LANs, a
separate ordinary client host on the mini's LAN, native macOS WebView media and
physical camera/microphone quality remain distinct acceptance cases.

New protocol capabilities such as true multiplexing, automatic federation trust,
mailbox-backed calling, TURN or stronger replicated-storage guarantees require
an explicit design and new evidence. They are not implied by the implemented
capabilities above.
# Performance requirements

Read this before changing background work, synchronization, storage, caches or UI
state. Mesh Talk should cost little while waiting, load data when needed and stay
bounded as history grows. This guide owns cross-cutting performance requirements;
[module ownership](module-boundaries.md), [network budgets](network-design-reference.md#8-resource-budgets-compatibility-and-performance)
and [reliability rules](ai-coding-reliability.md) own their implementation contracts.

## Budgets and measurement

These are initial project targets, **not industry standards or claims that the
current application meets them**. Establish a production-build baseline on each
supported platform. Reference fixture: 4 logical CPUs, 8 GiB RAM, SSD, 100 contacts,
20 groups and 100,000 stored messages; no pending transfers, calls or animations.
Separate cold start, warm start, catch-up, visible idle and hidden idle. Measure a
quiet five-minute window after warmup; record build, runtime, profile and workload.
Warm startup restarts the process with OS caches retained; cold startup records
its uncached/first-launch conditions. Usable means an actionable list or
conversation, not a blank shell; report human authorization waits separately.
The empty-shell comparison keeps the same backend, runtime, process membership
and window settings, with user payloads absent.

| Resource                | Initial target for the reference fixture                                                                                                                                                            |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Idle CPU                | Visible desktop: ≤1% of one logical CPU; hidden desktop: ≤0.25%; headless node: ≤0.5%, averaged over the window.                                                                                    |
| Retained memory         | Headless node: ≤64 MiB private commit. Desktop: ≤64 MiB workload delta above the same-build empty shell; establish a reviewed whole-family ceiling from that baseline.                              |
| Memory growth           | Repeated navigation/media cycles reach a bounded plateau. Tenfold stored history must not require tenfold startup reads or retained UI payloads.                                                    |
| Idle writes             | Zero business-data commits for unchanged inputs. Target ≤5 MiB/hour OS-observed attributable storage writes per application family after warmup; measure the full hour before claiming this target. |
| Background wakeups      | No application maintenance timer without pending work, a real deadline or a documented recovery purpose. Noncritical recovery defaults to ≥5 minutes and coalesces activation.                      |
| Startup and interaction | First usable shell ≤1 s warm / ≤3 s cold; ordinary interaction must not run blocking I/O, crypto or an unbounded traversal on the UI thread. Report hydration/catch-up separately.                  |

CPU means `100 × process CPU seconds / wall seconds`, summed over the full app
family; divide by logical CPU count only when reporting whole-machine percent.
Report Rust host **and** renderer/GPU/helpers. Distinguish private commit, private
resident memory, shared pages and live JS heap; on Linux use PSS for shared-page
attribution. Logical I/O includes IPC/network activity and is not physical disk
I/O; OS disk events also do not measure physical NAND write amplification. CPU alone does not establish battery/power efficiency: inspect wakeups, GPU,
network and actual energy where supported. Keep metrics collected in different
windows separate. Store measurements in PR/CI artifacts, not this guide.

An existing target miss requires recorded baseline and an owned follow-up; it is
not permission to worsen the path or silently raise its budget. A target change
requires comparable evidence and review. Migrations, catch-up and active media have
separate bounded work budgets and progress evidence, not an unlimited exception.

## Apply to every feature

Before implementation, identify the owning producer, its meaningful trigger,
bounded work unit, retained resources and stop condition. Review all three phases,
including costs introduced in another process or on another device:

| Phase           | Required design and evidence                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Startup         | Load indexed summaries and the active conversation's bounded page first. Defer inactive history, attachment bytes and optional features until demanded. Avoid decrypting all history, rebuilding unchanged indexes or republishing unchanged state at each login. Measure time to usable UI, peak memory, bytes read and writes separately from catch-up; migrations need resumable bounded progress.                    |
| Idle            | With unchanged inputs, settle business producers and avoid business-data writes. Use scoped events and exact next deadlines; coalesce noncritical repair into the existing serial queue, normally at least five minutes apart. A heartbeat, read, empty reply or offline device must not restart historical work. Verify visible and hidden states, including renderer/helpers and remote work triggered by this client. |
| Active business | Bound each query, decrypt, decode, transfer and rendering turn by items and bytes. Drain real available work promptly with backpressure and cancellation; user interaction and reception must remain responsive. Measure latency, peak CPU/memory and I/O for send/receive, catch-up, search, media and navigation as applicable, then prove resources settle when work finishes.                                        |

Do not classify a permanently retrying historical queue as an unlimited active
workload. Distinguish actionable progress from blocked work, record its outcome
and retain a bounded retry deadline. Successful reads, metadata comparisons and
already-held custody are not new user data. Serializing unnecessary work or
lengthening a timer alone does not establish that its cost is justified.

For every affected phase, the PR must state the trigger and stop condition,
resource bound, selected regression and measured result or explicit evidence gap.
Exercise unchanged inputs, growing history, unavailable dependencies and owner
replacement where applicable. Compare the same workload before and after; verify
return to idle and memory reclamation after repeated use. Do not infer low power
from a quiet disk, fast startup from a blank window, or bounded memory from one
snapshot. Existing misses remain explicit follow-ups with an owning module and
reproduction; never describe a passing correctness test as performance acceptance.

## Design and review rules

1. **Trigger work from meaning.** Prefer committed changes, scoped invalidations,
   user navigation and foreground activation. Schedule the next actual expiry or
   retry deadline. Empty success is not progress and must not keep a fast retry
   hot. Coalesce duplicate wakes; retain bounded dirty work while a task is busy.
   Pending work still owns its retry deadline. Suppress unchanged ordinary wakes
   using scheduling evidence, independently of successful completion; preserve
   explicit drivers and event-only progress when no timer owns continuation.
   A retained blocked task is not evidence of progress: keep its recovery fact
   while backing off, and resume promptly on dependency changes. Local pagination
   and actual received bytes retain prompt continuation.
   Reconfirming an already-held relay copy is not new progress. Park unchanged
   successful reconciliation until sparse repair; keep authenticated recipient
   delivery and actual custody-loss recovery separate from that scheduling hint.
   A bounded historical scan must also become quiet after its complete sweep;
   preserve prompt unfinished pages and separate lightweight claim rechecks.
   Qualify scan completion against current source and semantic inputs, before
   and after work. Failed discovery keeps a separate bounded wait; it cannot
   acknowledge EOF or repeatedly hydrate the same blocked item on observer wakes.
   Preserve invalidation domains through batching and acknowledgement; a roster
   heartbeat must not reload unrelated settings or history. Empty pages do not
   imply a global change. Presentation metadata does not renew user activity.
## Validation stages and agent responsibilities

Validation depth and business capability are separate dimensions. Use the same
owning contracts at each depth; a development result never promotes itself into
candidate acceptance. This follows staged pipelines and actionable feedback as
described by [Fowler](https://martinfowler.com/bliki/DeploymentPipeline.html) and
[Software Engineering at Google](https://abseil.io/resources/swe-book/html/ch23.html).

| Stage                | Trigger and purpose                                                                          | Entry or evidence                                                                    |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Understand and plan  | Start work or change its scope; identify business owner, consumers and obligations           | Owning guides, `make verify-plan`                                                    |
| Change feedback      | Validate a small change with affected static checks and executable tests                     | `make verify-changed`, development feedback JSON                                     |
| Boundary validation  | Change cross-module interfaces, runtime IPC, visible behavior, persistence or lifecycle      | Plan requirements and escalation review; focused integration/browser/native evidence |
| Candidate acceptance | Accept the current committed PR head before merge                                            | Required protected CI; optional local `prepare-pr.sh` and full health                |
| Extended validation  | Scheduled, release or explicitly triggered compatibility, stress and long-running properties | Owning backend/UI/native workflows and evaluation guides                             |

Read the selected capability's authoritative guide before changing behavior.
Declare semantic risks that source imports cannot express, inspect automatic
consumers and boundary requirements, and add missing owners/scenarios with a
reason. AI may expand scope; it cannot remove mandatory selections because it
judges a change low risk. Preserve the distinction between local acceptance,
recipient delivery and read state, and between frontend ownership and host
session authority. Summarize observed results and remaining obligations before
moving to candidate acceptance.

## Maintaining standards across requirements

# Implementation status and acceptance boundaries

This stable path is the current status index, not a chronological TODO list or a
claim that every topology/platform combination has been verified. Feature and
protocol details belong to the linked owning guides; Git history records completed
work.

## Current capability areas

| Area                       | Implemented behavior                                                                                                                             | Reference / boundary                                                                                                                                                                    |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Direct conversations       | Signed discovery, identity-pinned Noise/TCP, encrypted account-addressed DMs, replies, reactions, mentions, search and retained history.         | [Architecture](../docs/ARCHITECTURE.md); discovery and TCP reachability remain separate.                                                                                                |
| Groups                     | Signed membership controls, sender-key encryption, bounded fanout and authorized member recovery with per-member sharing.                        | [Group flows and scenarios](../docs/network-design-reference.md#d-group-creation-distribution-and-member-recovery); a removed/nonmember device cannot acquire authority from discovery. |
| Relay networking           | Equal trusted post offices, shared public enrollment, opaque custody/federation, direct-first attempts, soft preference and alternatives.        | [Network baseline](../docs/network-design-reference.md); an alternate needs a surviving onward route.                                                                                   |
| Network controls           | Per-device master/send/receive/directory preferences, physical-LAN-only discovery and direct LAN/Tailscale relay selection.                      | [Privacy controls](../docs/privacy-controls.md); visibility does not grant conversation authority or create a firewall.                                                                 |
| Files and folders          | Encrypted chunks, exact-offer consent, durable decisions, restart recovery, integrity checks and recipient completion.                           | [File flow](../docs/network-design-reference.md#e-files-folders-consent-and-completion); card arrival is not byte completion.                                                           |
| Linked devices             | Code-authorized enrollment, certified sibling synchronization and device-local category preferences.                                             | [Pairing and replay](../docs/network-design-reference.md#g-linking-and-ongoing-account-synchronization); full replay needs its own live authenticated route.                            |
| Calls                      | Optional device-addressed live Noise signaling and separate WebRTC media.                                                                        | No post-office signaling fallback or TURN service; native WebView and physical capture acceptance remain separate.                                                                      |
| Desktop presentation       | Shared person/relay classification, account/device profile details, themes, avatars, stickers, virtualized navigation and optional pack installation. | [Visual system](../frontend/DESIGN.md) · [Customization packs](../docs/CUSTOMIZATION_PACKS.md).                                                                                         |
| Local privacy and recovery | Privacy presets, lock controls, hidden contacts, local retention, recall and encrypted manual backup/restore.                                    | [Privacy](../docs/privacy-controls.md) · [Backup/recovery](../docs/backup-recovery.md); restore creates a new device and cannot revoke an old one.                                      |

## Deliberate design boundaries

- **Pairing authorization:** a one-time 128-bit code binds the linker and joiner
  device keys. Durable enrollment invalidates old sessions; interrupted adoption
  has a restricted code-authenticated retry. There is no separate SAS ceremony.
- **Relay metadata:** production relays store opaque outer events, not readable
  original authors, conversation IDs or channel controls. Connection identities,
  pseudonymous mailboxes, size buckets and timing remain observable. See
  [the exact privacy boundary](../docs/post-office-metadata-privacy.md).
- **Bounded custody:** relay copies have capacity limits and a 30-day maximum age;
  this is not guaranteed minimum retention or permanent storage.
- **Connections:** the client Node has bounded sequential session reuse, not one
  multiplexed socket per relay or an eight-socket ceiling for the whole machine.
- **Reachability and trust:** Tailscale does not merge LANs; explicit relay trust
  and client directory consent are independent of routing.
- **Membership presentation:** removed group members' past reactions no longer
  render under the current-membership visibility rule.
- **Linux dependency constraint:** the maintained
  [GLib compatibility workflow](../.github/workflows/glib-0.20-watch.yml) tracks the
  GTK/Tauri dependency gate. Consult the lockfile and security configuration before
  changing versions; do not treat this note as a vulnerability waiver.

## Evidence and future decisions

The [implementation/evidence tracker](../docs/network-design-reference.md#implementation-and-evidence-tracker)
records named logical and physical checks. Three independent physical LANs, a
separate ordinary client host on the mini's LAN, native macOS WebView media and
physical camera/microphone quality remain distinct acceptance cases.

New protocol capabilities such as true multiplexing, automatic federation trust,
mailbox-backed calling, TURN or stronger replicated-storage guarantees require
an explicit design and new evidence. They are not implied by the implemented
capabilities above.
# Performance requirements

Read this before changing background work, synchronization, storage, caches or UI
state. Mesh Talk should cost little while waiting, load data when needed and stay
bounded as history grows. This guide owns cross-cutting performance requirements;
[module ownership](module-boundaries.md), [network budgets](network-design-reference.md#8-resource-budgets-compatibility-and-performance)
and [reliability rules](ai-coding-reliability.md) own their implementation contracts.

## Budgets and measurement

These are initial project targets, **not industry standards or claims that the
current application meets them**. Establish a production-build baseline on each
supported platform. Reference fixture: 4 logical CPUs, 8 GiB RAM, SSD, 100 contacts,
20 groups and 100,000 stored messages; no pending transfers, calls or animations.
Separate cold start, warm start, catch-up, visible idle and hidden idle. Measure a
quiet five-minute window after warmup; record build, runtime, profile and workload.
Warm startup restarts the process with OS caches retained; cold startup records
its uncached/first-launch conditions. Usable means an actionable list or
conversation, not a blank shell; report human authorization waits separately.
The empty-shell comparison keeps the same backend, runtime, process membership
and window settings, with user payloads absent.

| Resource                | Initial target for the reference fixture                                                                                                                                                            |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Idle CPU                | Visible desktop: ≤1% of one logical CPU; hidden desktop: ≤0.25%; headless node: ≤0.5%, averaged over the window.                                                                                    |
| Retained memory         | Headless node: ≤64 MiB private commit. Desktop: ≤64 MiB workload delta above the same-build empty shell; establish a reviewed whole-family ceiling from that baseline.                              |
| Memory growth           | Repeated navigation/media cycles reach a bounded plateau. Tenfold stored history must not require tenfold startup reads or retained UI payloads.                                                    |
| Idle writes             | Zero busin…334 tokens truncated…acts, not this guide.

An existing target miss requires recorded baseline and an owned follow-up; it is
not permission to worsen the path or silently raise its budget. A target change
requires comparable evidence and review. Migrations, catch-up and active media have
separate bounded work budgets and progress evidence, not an unlimited exception.

## Apply to every feature

Before implementation, identify the owning producer, its meaningful trigger,
bounded work unit, retained resources and stop condition. Review all three phases,
including costs introduced in another process or on another device:

| Phase           | Required design and evidence                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Startup         | Load indexed summaries and the active conversation's bounded page first. Defer inactive history, attachment bytes and optional features until demanded. Avoid decrypting all history, rebuilding unchanged indexes or republishing unchanged state at each login. Measure time to usable UI, peak memory, bytes read and writes separately from catch-up; migrations need resumable bounded progress.                    |
| Idle            | With unchanged inputs, settle business producers and avoid business-data writes. Use scoped events and exact next deadlines; coalesce noncritical repair into the existing serial queue, normally at least five minutes apart. A heartbeat, read, empty reply or offline device must not restart historical work. Verify visible and hidden states, including renderer/helpers and remote work triggered by this client. |
| Active business | Bound each query, decrypt, decode, transfer and rendering turn by items and bytes. Drain real available work promptly with backpressure and cancellation; user interaction and reception must remain responsive. Measure latency, peak CPU/memory and I/O for send/receive, catch-up, search, media and navigation as applicable, then prove resources settle when work finishes.                                        |

Do not classify a permanently retrying historical queue as an unlimited active
workload. Distinguish actionable progress from blocked work, record its outcome
and retain a bounded retry deadline. Successful reads, metadata comparisons and
already-held custody are not new user data. Serializing unnecessary work or
lengthening a timer alone does not establish that its cost is justified.

For every affected phase, the PR must state the trigger and stop condition,
resource bound, selected regression and measured result or explicit evidence gap.
Exercise unchanged inputs, growing history, unavailable dependencies and owner
replacement where applicable. Compare the same workload before and after; verify
return to idle and memory reclamation after repeated use. Do not infer low power
from a quiet disk, fast startup from a blank window, or bounded memory from one
snapshot. Existing misses remain explicit follow-ups with an owning module and
reproduction; never describe a passing correctness test as performance acceptance.

## Design and review rules

1. **Trigger work from meaning.** Prefer committed changes, scoped invalidations,
   user navigation and foreground activation. Schedule the next actual expiry or
   retry deadline. Empty success is not progress and must not keep a fast retry
   hot. Coalesce duplicate wakes; retain bounded dirty work while a task is busy.
   Pending work still owns its retry deadline. Suppress unchanged ordinary wakes
   using scheduling evidence, independently of successful completion; preserve
   explicit drivers and event-only progress when no timer owns continuation.
   A retained blocked task is not evidence of progress: keep its recovery fact
   while backing off, and resume promptly on dependency changes. Local pagination
   and actual received bytes retain prompt continuation.
   Reconfirming an already-held relay copy is not new progress. Park unchanged
   successful reconciliation until sparse repair; keep authenticated recipient
   delivery and actual custody-loss recovery separate from that scheduling hint.
   A bounded historical scan must also become quiet after its complete sweep;
   preserve prompt unfinished pages and separate lightweight claim rechecks.
   Qualify scan completion against current source and semantic inputs, before
   and after work. Failed discovery keeps a separate bounded wait; it cannot
   acknowledge EOF or repeatedly hydrate the same blocked item on observer wakes.
   Preserve invalidation domains through batching and acknowledgement; a roster
   heartbeat must not reload unrelated settings or history. Empty pages do not
   imply a global change. Presentation metadata does not renew user activity.
## Validation stages and agent responsibilities

Validation depth and business capability are separate dimensions. Use the same
owning contracts at each depth; a development result never promotes itself into
candidate acceptance. This follows staged pipelines and actionable feedback as
described by [Fowler](https://martinfowler.com/bliki/DeploymentPipeline.html) and
[Software Engineering at Google](https://abseil.io/resources/swe-book/html/ch23.html).

| Stage                | Trigger and purpose                                                                          | Entry or evidence                                                                    |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Understand and plan  | Start work or change its scope; identify business owner, consumers and obligations           | Owning guides, `make verify-plan`                                                    |
| Change feedback      | Validate a small change with affected static checks and executable tests                     | `make verify-changed`, development feedback JSON                                     |
| Boundary validation  | Change cross-module interfaces, runtime IPC, visible behavior, persistence or lifecycle      | Plan requirements and escalation review; focused integration/browser/native evidence |
| Candidate acceptance | Accept the current committed PR head before merge                                            | Required protected CI; optional local `prepare-pr.sh` and full health                |
| Extended validation  | Scheduled, release or explicitly triggered compatibility, stress and long-running properties | Owning backend/UI/native workflows and evaluation guides                             |

Read the selected capability's authoritative guide before changing behavior.
Declare semantic risks that source imports cannot express, inspect automatic
consumers and boundary requirements, and add missing owners/scenarios with a
reason. AI may expand scope; it cannot remove mandatory selections because it
judges a change low risk. Preserve the distinction between local acceptance,
recipient delivery and read state, and between frontend ownership and host
session authority. Summarize observed results and remaining obligations before
moving to candidate acceptance.
